metadata.name: @scale-ds/scale-design-system
metadata.description: Scale Design System tokens in W3C Design Tokens Community Group format

in-out.$description: A tuned "standard" curve, a fast-out-slow-in: it reaches 0.776 at its midpoint, not 0.5. NOT the same as the CSS `ease-in-out` keyword (0.42, 0, 0.58, 1), which is symmetric, and not the same as Figma's "Ease In And Out", which matches the keyword. Use easing.in-out-sine or easing.in-out-quad when you need real symmetry.

emphasized.$description: A headline curve for hero moments. Defined as a two-segment path, not a cubic-bezier; sampled here so it can be used exactly. Sampled linear() curve. Neither DTCG nor Tokens Studio has a type for multi-point easing, so this ships as a string. It cannot round-trip to Figma as a named ease, and in After Effects or Lottie it is a multi-keyframe construction, not an ease.

spring-subtle.$description: SPATIAL ONLY — springs overshoot past their target, which is meaningless for opacity and colour. Figma parameterises springs by mass/stiffness/damping and its preset values are unpublished, so there is no exact Figma equivalent; match by eye against Gentle/Quick/Bouncy. Sampled linear() curve. Neither DTCG nor Tokens Studio has a type for multi-point easing, so this ships as a string. It cannot round-trip to Figma as a named ease, and in After Effects or Lottie it is a multi-keyframe construction, not an ease.

spin.$description: Looping animation shorthand. No DTCG or Tokens Studio type covers an iteration count, so this is `other`. Pair with the `sc-motion-<name>` keyframe.

pulse.$description: Looping animation shorthand. No DTCG or Tokens Studio type covers an iteration count, so this is `other`. Pair with the `sc-motion-<name>` keyframe.

slide.$description: Default travel for the slide keyframes, overridden on the animating element — set it to {motion.distance.full} on a drawer. Not a design decision on its own; it is the knob the eight slide keyframes read so magnitude need not be baked into their names.
